questions.question: The transformation scheme turns a maximization linear program, with constraints of type $\leq$, $\geq$ or $=$ and variables that are nonnegative, nonpositive or free, into a minimization dual. Which description of that dual is correct?
options: Constraints $\leq,\geq,=$ give $y_i\leq0$, $y_i\geq0$, $y_i\in\mathbb{R}$; variables $x_j\geq0$, $x_j\leq0$, $x_j\in\mathbb{R}$ give dual constraints $\leq,\geq,=$
Constraints $\leq,\geq,=$ give dual constraints $\geq,\leq,=$; variables $x_j\geq0$, $x_j\leq0$, $x_j\in\mathbb{R}$ give dual variables $y_j\geq0$, $y_j\leq0$, $y_j\in\mathbb{R}$
Constraints $\leq,\geq,=$ give $y_i\geq0$, $y_i\leq0$, $y_i\in\mathbb{R}$; variables $x_j\geq0$, $x_j\leq0$, $x_j\in\mathbb{R}$ give dual constraints $\geq,\leq,=$
Constraints $\leq,\geq,=$ give $y_i\geq0$, $y_i\leq0$, $y_i\in\mathbb{R}$; every variable $x_j$, whatever its sign, gives a dual constraint $\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq c_j$

questions.question: A maximization linear program contains the constraint $7\geq x_1-2x_2$, written with the constant on the left. Which sign condition does the transformation scheme give its dual variable $y$?
options: $y\geq0$, because the constraint reads $x_1-2x_2\leq7$ once the variables are on the left
$y\leq0$, because the constraint is written with the symbol $\geq$ in a maximization program
$y\leq0$, because moving the constant to the right turns it into $x_1-2x_2\geq7$
$y\in\mathbb{R}$, because the constant may stand on either side, so no direction is fixed

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ and $\boldsymbol{c}\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Using the transformation table, what is the dual of the symmetric-form program $\min\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$?
options: $\max\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c}$, $\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\max\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{c}$, $\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\min\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c}$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\max\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{c}$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$

questions.question: A maximization linear program has three constraints, of types $\leq$, $\geq$ and $=$, and four variables: two nonnegative, one nonpositive and one free. How many variables and constraints does the dual written with the transformation scheme have?
options: Four dual variables and five dual constraints, after splitting the equality and the free variable
Three dual variables and four dual constraints, exactly one of which is an equality
Four dual variables and three dual constraints, exactly one of which is an equality
Three dual variables and four dual constraints, exactly two of which are equalities

questions.question: For $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ with constraints $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq b_i$, $\geq b_i$ or $=b_i$, the dual adds the constraints with weights $y_i$ to bound the objective from above. Which sign must the weight of a constraint $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\geq b_i$ have, and why?
options: $y_i\geq0$: then $y_i\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\geq y_ib_i$, and adding it gives an upper bound on the objective
$y_i\in\mathbb{R}$: the constraint can be rewritten as $-\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq-b_i$, so either sign works
$y_i\leq0$: then $y_i\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq y_ib_i$, an upper estimate that can be added to the others
$y_i=0$: a $\geq$ constraint only bounds $\boldsymbol{x}$ from below, so it never limits a maximum

questions.question: A maximization program with one equality constraint reads $\max Z=3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq4$, $x_1+3x_2=6$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$. What is its dual according to the transformation table?
options: $\min 4y_1+6y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\geq3$, $y_1+3y_2\geq2$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\geq0$
$\min 4y_1+6y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\geq3$, $y_1+3y_2\geq2$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\in\mathbb{R}$
$\min 4y_1+6y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\geq3$, $y_1+3y_2\geq2$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\leq0$

questions.question: In $\max Z=x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq5$, $-x_1+x_2\leq1$, $x_1\in\mathbb{R}$, $x_2\geq0$, the dual variables of the two constraints are $y_1,y_2$. Which dual constraint belongs to the free variable $x_1$, and which signs do $y_1,y_2$ get?
options: $y_1-y_2\geq1$, with $y_1\geq0$ and $y_2\geq0$
$y_1+y_2=1$, with $y_1\geq0$ and $y_2\geq0$
$y_1-y_2\geq1$, with $y_1\in\mathbb{R}$ and $y_2\geq0$
$y_1-y_2=1$, with $y_1\geq0$ and $y_2\geq0$

questions.question: The program $\min 4x_1+5x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\geq6$, $3x_1+x_2\leq9$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$ is dualized with the transformation scheme, with $y_1,y_2$ for the two constraints. Which sign conditions do $y_1$ and $y_2$ get?
options: $y_1\geq0$ and $y_2\leq0$
$y_1\leq0$ and $y_2\geq0$
$y_1\geq0$ and $y_2\geq0$
$y_1\leq0$ and $y_2\leq0$

questions.question: For $\min 3x_1-2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\geq2$, $2x_1-x_2\leq8$, $x_1\geq0$, $x_2\leq0$, with dual variables $y_1,y_2$ for the two constraints, which dual constraint does the transformation scheme give for the nonpositive variable $x_2$?

The program $\min 8y_1+y_2$ subject to $2y_1-2y_2\geq4$, $3y_1+y_2=2$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\leq0$ is the scheme's dual of a maximization program in $x_1,x_2$ whose constraints 1 and 2 belong to $y_1$ and $y_2$. Which constraint types and variable signs does that maximization program have?
options: Constraint 1 is $\geq$, constraint 2 is $\leq$; $x_1\leq0$ and $x_2\in\mathbb{R}$
Constraint 1 is $\geq$, constraint 2 is $=$; $x_1\geq0$ and $x_2\leq0$
Constraint 1 is $\leq$, constraint 2 is $\geq$; $x_1\leq0$ and $x_2\in\mathbb{R}$
Constraint 1 is $\leq$, constraint 2 is $\geq$; $x_1\geq0$ and $x_2\in\mathbb{R}$

questions.question: In $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, every variable is nonnegative except $x_j$, which is free and is replaced by $x_j=x_j^{+}-x_j^{-}$ with $x_j^{+},x_j^{-}\geq0$. What do the dual constraints of $x_j^{+}$ and $x_j^{-}$ in the standard-form dual give together?
options: $\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq c_j$ and $-\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq-c_j$, which together say $\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i=c_j$
$\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq c_j$ twice, since the column of $x_j^{-}$ is a copy of the column of $x_j^{+}$
$\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq c_j$ and $\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq-c_j$, which together say $\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq|c_j|$
No new relation; instead the two weights merge into one free dual variable $y_j$ for $x_j$

questions.question: For $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ with weights $\boldsymbol{y}$ of the correct signs, the bound $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ needs $\big(\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\big)x_j\geq c_jx_j$ for every allowed value of each $x_j$. If $x_j\leq0$, which dual constraint does this require?
options: $\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\geq c_j$, the relation used for every variable of a maximization program
$\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i=c_j$, because a variable that can be negative has to be treated as free
No dual constraint for $x_j$; instead the dual variable $y_j$ has to be nonpositive
$\sum_ia_{i,j}y_i\leq c_j$, because multiplying by $x_j\leq0$ reverses the inequality

questions.question: In a maximization program the constraint $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=b_i$ is replaced by $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq b_i$ and $-\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq-b_i$, with nonnegative standard-form weights $u_i$ and $v_i$. How do $u_i,v_i$ enter the dual, and what follows for the equality's dual variable $y_i$?
options: Only through $u_i+v_i\geq0$, so the equality's dual variable $y_i$ is nonnegative
Only through $u_i-v_i$, which takes every real value, so $y_i=u_i-v_i$ is free
Through $u_i+v_i$ in the dual objective and $u_i-v_i$ in the dual constraints, so no single $y_i$ replaces them
Their contributions cancel, so an equality constraint leaves no dual variable at all

questions.question: For the minimization program with a free variable $\min 3x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\geq4$, $x_1-x_2=1$, $x_1\geq0$, $x_2\in\mathbb{R}$, which maximization program does the scheme produce as the dual?
options: $\max 4y_1+y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\geq3$, $y_1-y_2=1$, $y_1\leq0$, $y_2\in\mathbb{R}$
$\max 4y_1+y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\leq3$, $y_1-y_2\leq1$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\in\mathbb{R}$
$\max 4y_1+y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\leq3$, $y_1-y_2=1$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\in\mathbb{R}$
$\max 4y_1+y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\leq3$, $y_1-y_2=1$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\geq0$

questions.question: For $\max Z=2x_1-3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq4$, $x_1-x_2\leq6$, $x_1\geq0$, $x_2\leq0$, which vector $\boldsymbol{y}=(y_1,y_2)$ is feasible for the dual linear program that the transformation scheme gives?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,5)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(2,0)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(3,-1)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(0,-3)$

questions.question: In $\max Z=2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\leq8$, $x_1\geq3$, $x_2\geq0$, the bound $x_1\geq3$ is treated as a second constraint with dual variable $y_2$, and $x_1$ is declared free. Which dual does the transformation scheme give?
options: $\min 8y_1+3y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2=2$, $2y_1\geq1$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\geq0$
$\min 8y_1+3y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2=2$, $2y_1\geq1$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\leq0$
$\min 8y_1-3y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2=2$, $2y_1\geq1$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\geq0$
$\min 8y_1+3y_2$ subject to $y_1+2y_2=2$, $y_1\geq1$, $y_1\geq0$, $y_2\leq0$

questions.question: To dualize $\min\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ (constraints of any type, variables of any sign), a student rewrites it as $\max\,-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, applies the transformation table's max column to get $\min\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{u}$ with dual constraints $\sum_ia_{i,j}u_i\ \square\ -c_j$, and substitutes $\boldsymbol{u}=-\boldsymbol{y}$. What does this produce?
options: The signs on $\boldsymbol{y}$ reverse, but the dual constraints keep the max-column relations, with right-hand side $\boldsymbol{c}$
The relations of the dual constraints reverse, but the sign conditions on $\boldsymbol{y}$ stay as in the max column
Only the objective changes, to $\max\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$; signs and relations stay as in the max column
Signs on $\boldsymbol{y}$ and dual-constraint relations both reverse, and the objective becomes $\max\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq10$, $x_1\geq5$ (kept as a constraint), $x_2\geq0$, student A declares $x_1\geq0$ and student B declares $x_1$ free. Their duals differ only in the dual constraint of $x_1$: $y_1+y_2\geq3$ for A, $y_1+y_2=3$ for B. Which statement about the two duals is correct?
options: Only B's is correct: with $x_1\geq5$ kept as a constraint, $x_1$ may not also be declared nonnegative
Only A's is correct: since $x_1\geq5$ forces $x_1\geq0$, declaring $x_1$ free misstates the program
Both are correct duals of programs with the same feasible set, and both have optimal value $30$
Both are correct duals, but B's optimal value is larger, as its equality shrinks the feasible set

questions.question: The program $\max Z=x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq6$, $x_1-x_2=2$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$ has optimal value $10$. A student gives the equality's dual variable the sign $y_2\geq0$ and writes $\min 6y_1+2y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\geq1$, $y_1-y_2\geq3$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$. What is the optimal value of the student's program?
options: $10$, equal to the primal optimum, since the sign of an equality's weight is irrelevant
$18$: each feasible point still bounds $Z$ from above, but the best bound exceeds $10$
$12$, obtained from the correct dual optimum $(2,-1)$ by setting its negative entry to $0$
None: the program is infeasible, because the correct dual optimum has $y_2<0$

questions.question: The program $\min 2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\geq2$, $x_1+2x_2\leq6$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$ has optimal value $4$. Reading the max column of the transformation table by mistake, a student writes $\max 2y_1+6y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\geq2$, $y_1+2y_2\geq3$, $y_1\leq0$, $y_2\geq0$. What happens to the student's program?
options: It is unbounded, so it cannot be the dual: a correct dual would have optimal value $4$
It is infeasible, which is the only outcome that reading the wrong column can produce
It has optimal value $4$, so the wrong column happens to give the right dual here
It has optimal value $12$ at $\boldsymbol{y}=(0,2)$, an upper bound on the primal value
